adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the loop `usernames.split(",").each` only adds users when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a record; non-existent usernames are silently ignored. The action then renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, which it likely will even when no members were added, so the API can report success with no effect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member returns 200 success even when removing a user who isn't in the group, making it a silent no-op

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code unconditionally does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then returns `success_json` if `group.save` succeeds. `delete` on an association is effectively idempotent and will not error if the user isn’t currently a member, so the endpoint will still return 200 in that case (silent no-op). Whether that’s undesirable is an API/semantics decision, not an objectively broken behavior based on the diff alone.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes specs that explicitly asserted silent success when adding/removing non-existent users (previously under `.update` incremental tests, e.g. "succeeds silently when adding non-existent users"). The new membership API (`Admin::GroupsController#add_members`) still silently ignores unknown usernames (`User.find_by_username` check with no error/else), but there is no replacement spec covering this behavior, so the contract for handling invalid usernames is no longer defined by tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test covers the rewritten public GroupsController#members endpoint and its new {members, meta:{total,limit,offset}} response envelope that the JS pagination depends on

The only added/modified specs are for `Admin::GroupsController` (`spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`); there is no spec added here for the public `GroupsController#members` response format, so this new contract is untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group-members.js sets the group as the members controller model, relying on findMembers mutating the group — a non-obvious coupling with no error state if the ajax call fails

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`, `setupController(controller, model)` sets `controller.set("model", model);` where `model` is the group, then calls `model.findMembers();` without using the returned promise. In `Discourse.Group#findMembers` (models/group.js) the AJAX response is applied via `self.setProperties({ ..., members: ... })`, and the template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` now renders `{{#each m in members}}`, implying reliance on that side-effectful mutation rather than the route providing a members collection. This is a real, diff-grounded coupling/architecture concern; additionally, there is no explicit error handling/state in the route if the AJAX call fails (the promise is ignored), though whether that manifests as a user-visible defect isn't provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Public group members page paginates at 50 with no pagination controls, making members beyond the first 50 unreachable; new groups_controller limit drops the 200-member default and caps every group at 50 where old code only paginated automatic groups

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, pagination is now always applied with a default `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset` (no longer only for `group.automatic?`, and no longer defaulting to 200). On the public group members route (`discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`), it calls `model.findMembers()` once but provides no actions/UI to change `offset`/`limit`, and the public template `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` adds no pagination controls. This makes members beyond the first page (default 50) unreachable compared to the old behavior where non-automatic groups were unpaginated (all members returned) and automatic groups defaulted to 200.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages computed as floor(user_count / limit) + 1 yields an empty phantom page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 100 members at limit 50 gives 3 pages, last empty)

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g. 100/50), this returns 3 instead of 2, creating a phantom last page. This is observable because `next` sets `offset` to `Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, allowing `offset == user_count` (e.g. 100), and `findMembers` then requests that offset and sets `members` from the response, which will be empty at `offset == total`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members silently drops unknown usernames while the API returns success_json; old tests documenting the silent behavior were deleted and the new spec only covers the happy path plus automatic-group rejection

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds users when `User.find_by_username` returns a record, otherwise it does nothing, yet it still renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds (which it likely will even if no users were added). That means unknown usernames are silently ignored with a success response. The prior spec suite explicitly covered this “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users” behavior under the old PATCH path, but those tests were removed and the new specs for `add_members` only cover the happy path (adding real users) and automatic-group rejection, leaving this specific edge behavior untested/documented for the new endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Scope drift into unrelated files: admin_base.scss extends .form-horizontal block to .badges untouched by the change, and admin-group-selector.hbs / user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs receive whitespace-only rewrites

Also `admin-group-selector.hbs` is modified only to remove blank lines, and `user-selector-autocomplete.raw.hbs` is largely indentation/whitespace reformatting with no apparent functional change. These are scope/cleanup concerns rather than a verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model.findMembers() is fire-and-forget in setupController instead of returned from afterModel, so route transition completes before member data exists, no loading state is tracked, and no error handling if the AJAX rejects

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `afterModel` (which previously `return`ed `model.findMembers()` and thus made the transition wait / route error handling kick in) and replaces it with a fire-and-forget call in `setupController` (`admin_group_route.js` and `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`: `model.findMembers();`). That means the route can render before `members` is populated (templates now iterate `members`), there’s no explicit loading state, and a rejected AJAX promise from `findMembers` won’t be propagated through Ember’s normal route promise chain/error hooks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member's group.users.delete followed by group.save succeeds silently for a non-member user_id, and group.save is a no-op after an association delete making the render_json_error branch dead code

adjudication.rationale:
In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the diff shows `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `if group.save ... else render_json_error(group)`.

For a typical AR `has_many :through`/HABTM association, `delete` issues the DELETE against the join table immediately; it is a no-op if the user isn’t a member, and it does not make `group` invalid. As written, the action will therefore return success even for a non-member `user_id`, and the `render_json_error` branch is very likely unreachable because `group.save` will usually succeed (or be unnecessary) after the association delete.

This is a real, diff-grounded concern about semantics/maintainability (and possibly API behavior expectations), but the diff alone doesn’t prove it violates a required contract, so it’s not clearly a verifiable bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers does not clear the usernames input after adding members (shipped TODO), so pressing Add again re-submits the same usernames and leaves ambiguous UI state

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `addMembers` action explicitly includes `// TODO: should clear the input` and never resets `this.get("usernames")` after calling `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));`. Since the template binds the user-selector to `usernames` (`{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}`), the input will retain the previous value, making repeated clicks resubmit the same usernames and leaving the UI state unclear. This is a real, diff-grounded UX/state-management issue, but not a hard correctness break proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking API contract change in admin groups create: new code reads top-level params[:name]/params[:visible] instead of the previous group: {name, usernames, visible} envelope, causing existing API callers' requests to fail validation or silently drop usernames, with no route/version bump

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows Admin::GroupsController#create was changed to read top-level params (`params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`) and no longer reads the previous `params[:group]` envelope or `usernames` (old code: `params[:group][:name]`, `params[:group][:usernames]`, etc.). The route remains the same `POST /admin/groups`, and membership is now handled via separate `PUT /admin/groups/:group_id/members` (`add_members`). Any existing caller still sending `{ group: { name, usernames, visible } }` would now result in `name` being blank (and likely failing save) and `usernames` being ignored. Whether this is an intentional API change or not isn’t provable from the diff, but the breaking contract aspect is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking API contract change in admin groups update: new code reads top-level params[:alias_level]/params[:visible]/params[:name] instead of group: {...} payload, silently ignoring nested payloads; PATCH requests with changes: {add/delete} now hit update which ignores changes entirely and returns success_json, silently dropping membership edits with a 200

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#update`, the diff removes the prior PATCH handling (`update_patch`) and now only updates `alias_level/visible/name` from top-level params, ignoring `params[:changes]` entirely and still returning `success_json` when `group.save` succeeds. Since Rails routes still accept PATCH for `update`, a PATCH request with `changes: { add/delete: ... }` will be silently ignored with a 200. Additionally, the controller no longer reads the nested `params[:group]` payload used previously, so requests still sending `group: { ... }` will be ignored without an explicit error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages calculation in group.js uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1, which is wrong when user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g., 100/50 yields 3 pages instead of 2), allowing the UI to advance to an empty page; should be Math.ceil

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `totalPages` in `admin-group.js.es6` as `Math.floor(this.get("user_count") / this.get("limit")) + 1`, which overcounts when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100/50 => 3). The `next` action can then advance `offset` up to `user_count` (`Math.min(..., user_count)`), and `Group.findMembers` will request `offset` equal to `user_count`, yielding an empty `members` page. Using `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (and likely clamping offset to `user_count - limit`) would avoid the empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member spec issues xhr :put but the route is delete 'members', so PUT routes to groups#add_members; the test passes only because add_members has the same automatic-group guard, meaning remove_member's automatic-group rejection is never actually tested

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` invokes the `remove_member` controller action directly (controller specs bypass Rails routing), so it does not “route to `groups#add_members`” despite the routes mapping PUT `/members` to `add_members` and DELETE `/members` to `remove_member` in `config/routes.rb`. Also, `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` does not branch on HTTP verb, so the automatic-group guard is still exercised even with a PUT in this spec.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members uses usernames.split(',') without stripping whitespace or reporting misses, so invalid usernames are silently skipped and success_json is returned even when zero users were added, leaving the admin UI with no error surface

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and looks up `User.find_by_username(username)` without `strip`/normalization. This means inputs like `"bob, alice"` will include a leading space for `" alice"` and fail to match a real username, causing members not to be added. Additionally, nonexistent/invalid usernames are silently skipped and the action still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds (which it likely will even if no users were added), providing no error feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller#members has no upper clamp on the limit param (limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i), so ?limit=1000000 materializes the entire membership plus a full count on every call, widening an unbounded surface previously capped at 200 for automatic groups

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new code applies pagination to all groups but sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` with no upper bound, and then executes `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. This makes `?limit=1000000` capable of fetching essentially the whole membership list (if total <= limit) and the action also always performs `total = group.users.count`. Previously, automatic groups were explicitly capped (`limit = (params[:limit] || 200).to_i` inside the `group.automatic?` branch). The diff therefore introduces/expands an unbounded request surface for automatic groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group.js domain model now doubles as pagination state container, with findMembers overwriting the server-serialized user_count attribute with result.meta.total, conflating a persisted attribute with list-pagination meta and risking crashes or stale state if a code path returns a bare array without meta

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, `Discourse.Group` is expanded to hold pagination state (`limit`, `offset`, `user_count`) and `findMembers()` now mutates the model via `setProperties({ user_count: result.meta.total, limit: ..., offset: ..., members: ... })`. That does conflate a general group attribute (`user_count`, also coming from serializers elsewhere) with pagination/meta from a specific members-list fetch, which is a legitimate architecture/scope concern. However, the specific claim about “crashes ... if a code path returns a bare array without meta” isn’t shown in this diff (the new endpoint always returns `meta`, and the only early exit returns `undefined`, not a bare array).

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin_group_route.js setupController neither returns nor catches the model.findMembers() promise, so a failed members fetch renders the page with zero members and no error indication, making 'fetch failed' indistinguishable from an empty group; same pattern in discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6

adjudication.rationale: In both `admin_group_route.js` and `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6`, the diff changes from returning `model.findMembers().then(...)` in `afterModel` to calling `model.findMembers();` in `setupController` without returning/handling the promise. Since `findMembers` performs an async `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` and sets `members` only on success, a failed request will leave `members` unset and the templates (`{{each member in members}}` / `{{#each m in members}}`) will render empty with no route error propagation—unlike the previous `afterModel` return which would surface rejections via Ember's route error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: config/routes.rb:49 — `get "users"` admin endpoint silently deleted, breaking existing API consumers with a 404 and no deprecation path

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `get "users"` under the admin `resources :groups` routes is removed and replaced with `delete "members"` and `put "members"` (config/routes.rb). That is a real, diff-grounded API surface change; however, the claim that it "breaks existing API consumers" cannot be verified from the diff (no evidence of external consumers or compatibility guarantees). The app code in this PR appears updated to use the new `/admin/groups/:id/members.json` endpoints, so it’s not a demonstrable functional bug within the codebase itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/groups_controller.rb — PATCH incremental membership change API (changes:{add:,delete:}) removed; PATCH requests now fall through to update_put and silently no-op with a 200 response

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the PATCH-specific incremental membership handler (`update_patch`) and the `update` action no longer branches on `request.patch?` (it always runs the new `update` logic). As a result, PATCH requests that previously sent `params[:changes]` (add/delete usernames) are now ignored: `update` only applies `alias_level`, `visible`, and (non-automatic) `name`, then returns `success_json` on save. This makes prior PATCH membership-change calls effectively no-op while still returning 200, since the default RESTful PATCH route still exists.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb:22–27 — default member page size dropped from 200 to 50 for all groups while the public members template has no pagination controls, so members beyond 50 are inaccessible

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes member fetching to always apply pagination with `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `members = group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`, whereas previously pagination (default 200) was only applied for `automatic?` groups and non-automatic groups returned the full ordered list. On the public side, `discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6` now calls `model.findMembers()` and `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` renders `{{#each m in members}}` but the diff adds no pagination controls/actions in the public members template/route/controller (pagination controls were added only to the admin group UI). Therefore, without `limit/offset` controls in the public UI, members beyond the first 50 would not be reachable from this view.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller_spec.rb — test issues xhr :put against remove_member, routing to add_members instead, so the real remove-member-on-automatic-group path is untested

adjudication.rationale: In this controller spec, `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...` invokes the `remove_member` action directly; it does not go through `config/routes.rb` and therefore will not “route to add_members instead.” The automatic-group guard in `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` (`return can_not_modify_automatic if group.automatic`) is still exercised by that test regardless of HTTP verb. While the verb mismatch means it’s not testing the real DELETE route wiring, the finding’s claim that it hits `add_members` / leaves the remove-member automatic path untested is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin-group.js.es6 addMembers — user-selector input never cleared after adding members (TODO ships in diff), enabling duplicate re-submits and stale text pollution

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6` the `addMembers` action explicitly notes `// TODO: should clear the input` and does not reset `this.get("usernames")` after calling `this.get("model").addMembers(...)`. Since the template binds the `user-selector` to `usernames` (`{{user-selector usernames=usernames ...}}`), the entered text will remain after adding members, enabling easy duplicate re-submits / stale text. This is a diff-grounded incomplete UX behavior rather than a verifiable functional break (server-side may safely ignore duplicates).

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin_group_route.js / group-members.js.es6 — setupController fires model.findMembers() fire-and-forget instead of returning the promise, causing transient empty states and a stale-response race on rapid navigation
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments flag that findMembers() is invoked asynchronously without being awaited/returned, making the controller proceed without member data and introducing race conditions (e.g., empty/stale state on navigation).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Pagination `limit` in GroupsController is taken from client params without an upper bound, and now applies to all groups via find_group, allowing a single request with ?limit=99999999 to dump the full member roster of any visible group, bypassing the intended 50-per-page cap; also makes meta.limit attacker-controlled breaking client-side totalPages math in admin-group.js.es6. Suggested fix: clamp to limit = [[limit, 1].max, 100].min

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff introduces `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and uses it directly in `group.users...limit(limit)` while also reflecting it back via `meta: { limit: limit }` (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb). There is no upper bound/clamp, so a client can request an arbitrarily large page (e.g. `?limit=99999999`) for any group they can `ensure_can_see!`, which defeats the intended pagination cap/default and can cause excessive data/performance impact. Because `meta.limit` is derived from the unbounded param, it is attacker-controlled and will be propagated into the Ember model via `findMembers` (`self.setProperties({ limit: result.meta.limit, ... })`), which can distort paging math such as `totalPages` in `admin-group.js.es6`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin::GroupsController add_members splits usernames on comma with no trimming and no reporting of unmatched names, so input like "alice, bob" silently adds only " bob" failing lookup, while the endpoint returns success_json regardless — silent partial-adds with a 200 response. Suggested fix: trim each username and return list of unresolved usernames

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and then `User.find_by_username(username)` without trimming whitespace. This means inputs like `"alice, bob"` will pass `" bob"` (leading space) to the lookup and can fail to match an existing user. The method also ignores unmatched usernames and still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, so the request can succeed (200) while only partially adding members.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec at spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:100-102 sends xhr :put to remove_member, which routes to add_members due to route verb mapping, so remove_member's automatic-group guard has zero real test coverage and could regress unnoticed

adjudication.rationale: In config/routes.rb, the admin group members endpoints are verb-mapped as `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` and `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. But the spec under `context ".remove_member"` uses `xhr :put, :remove_member, ...`, which is not the verb that would reach `remove_member` via routing (PUT would be routed to `add_members`). While controller specs invoke the action directly (so it still executes `remove_member` and its automatic-group guard), this test does not validate the real routed behavior/HTTP method and could miss routing/verb regressions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec at spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb:57-64 drops coverage of the new flat-param update path for a normal group (params[:alias_level], params[:visible], name assignment), leaving the changed update contract untested; regressions like visible string/boolean mismatch or alias_level coercion would be invisible to the suite

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Admin::GroupsController#update` to read flat params (`params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]`) instead of the previous nested `params[:group]` payload. In `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, the prior normal-group update coverage (including members/name changes via nested params) is removed, and the remaining `.update` spec only asserts behavior for an *automatic* group (ignoring name change, setting visible). There is no spec exercising the new flat-param update path for a non-automatic group (e.g., alias_level coercion via `to_i`, visible string-to-boolean via `== "true"`, and name assignment when `!group.automatic`). This is a concrete, diff-created test gap rather than a direct runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb remove_member uses group.users.delete(user_id), bypassing the user_count counter cache maintained by group.add/group.remove; the subsequent group.save persists the stale user_count, causing pagination meta.total and admin UI totalPages/currentPage to drift out of sync (extra empty page, showingLast never triggers) until the count is recalculated

adjudication.rationale: The finding’s claimed UI/pagination drift via `meta.total` isn’t supported by the diff: `GroupsController#members` now sets `meta.total` from `group.users.count` (a fresh count query), and the JS `findMembers()` overwrites `user_count` from that `meta.total`, so admin `totalPages/currentPage` are driven by the live count returned by the members endpoint, not by any persisted `group.user_count` counter cache. While `group.users.delete(user_id)` may or may not bypass any custom `group.remove` logic/counter-cache (not shown in this diff), the specific broken behavior described cannot be verified from the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members in admin/groups_controller.rb silently skips unknown usernames and unconditionally renders success, so admins get a 200 even when users weren't added

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, unknown usernames are skipped (`if user = User.find_by_username(username) ... end`) and the action returns `success_json` whenever `group.save` succeeds, with no indication that some/all usernames were invalid. However, it’s not strictly “unconditional” (it depends on `group.save`), and the diff doesn’t prove this is a correctness defect vs. an intentional UX choice (prior specs show similar silent-success behavior for non-existent users).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Usernames split on ',' without .strip, so whitespace or trailing commas produce empty/failed lookups that are silently dropped

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` and then `User.find_by_username(username)` without trimming (`strip`) or rejecting blanks. This means inputs like `"alice, bob"` or `"alice,"` will yield `" bob"` / `""`, causing failed lookups that are silently ignored (`if user = ...`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: group.js addMembers/removeMember use Discourse.ajax(...).then with no rejection handler, so failed add/remove operations show no user-visible feedback

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js, both removeMember and addMembers call Discourse.ajax(...).then(function() { self.findMembers(); }) and do not attach any .catch/.fail handler. The diff also doesn’t show any UI-level error handling around the controller actions that call these methods. While this isn’t a proven “broken behavior” (Discourse.ajax may have global error handling), it is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness/UX gap: failures won’t trigger any local recovery or feedback path in these methods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers with next/previous sets offset before the request with no in-flight guard, allowing out-of-order responses to overwrite newer state and failed requests to leave offset desynced from the member list

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, the `next`/`previous` actions mutate pagination state (`group.set("offset", offset)`) before issuing the async request (`return group.findMembers();`). In `group.js`, `findMembers()` then asynchronously `setProperties({ offset: result.meta.offset, members: ... })` when the AJAX call resolves. Because there is no in-flight request tracking/cancellation, multiple rapid `next`/`previous` clicks can issue overlapping requests whose responses may resolve out of order and overwrite `members/offset` with stale page data. Also, if the AJAX request fails, the already-updated `offset` will remain changed while `members` stays on the previous list, leaving the UI state desynced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member performs a meaningless group.save after association delete whose failure renders a confusing 422 for an operation that succeeded

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then checks `if group.save` to decide whether to return success vs `render_json_error(group)` with a 422. The association deletion (`users.delete`) already applies the change to the join table; a subsequent `group.save` is unnecessary and could fail due to unrelated validations on `Group`, causing a 422 error response even though the member was actually removed. This matches the finding and is directly grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: members endpoint accepts unbounded/negative limit values with no clamp, returning bogus meta.limit or huge queries

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new pagination parameters are taken directly from the request without validation/clamping: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, then used in `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)` and echoed back in `meta.limit`/`meta.offset`. This allows negative or extremely large `limit` (and negative `offset`) values, which can result in unbounded/huge queries (e.g., PostgreSQL `LIMIT -1`) or invalid SQL, and returns bogus meta values. The diff introduces this behavior by adding `limit/offset` support for the members endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin group add-members input is never cleared after a successful add (acknowledged TODO), enabling accidental duplicate submissions

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the add-members action does not clear the input after adding: `actions.addMembers` in `admin-group.js.es6` has an explicit `// TODO: should clear the input` and calls `this.get("model").addMembers(this.get("usernames"));` without resetting `usernames` to empty/null. This is a real, diff-grounded UX/completeness issue (could lead to accidental repeated submissions), but it isn’t a verifiable correctness break since the request still succeeds and the server likely de-dupes membership.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Route setupController fires findMembers() without handling its rejection, leaving the members area empty indefinitely on transient failure with no retry

adjudication.rationale: In both `admin_group_route.js` and `group-members.js.es6`, `setupController` now calls `model.findMembers();` without returning/awaiting the promise or attaching error handling. `Discourse.Group#findMembers` only populates `members` inside the `.then(...)` of the AJAX call, so if the request fails/rejects, `members` never gets set and the templates (`{{each member in members}}` / `{{#each m in members}}`) will render nothing with no route-level error/transition handling. Previously `afterModel` returned the promise, allowing Ember’s route error handling to engage rather than silently leaving the UI empty.
